original.target_description: First condition, Figure 3 panel A: wrong crowd-size image selection by college degree versus less education among Trump voters/supporters; difference-of-proportions test. High education means at least a college degree; low education means some college or less.

n.location: Journal pp. 139–141 (PDF pp. 5–7), Figure 2 caption and Figure 3 discussion/caption
n.sample_role: Participants who voted for Trump, compared by educational attainment in the first crowd-size condition; education-subgroup analytic counts are not printed.
n.exclusions: Third-party voters excluded from vote-choice analyses; education-test-specific missingness/exclusions not documented.

es.location: Journal p. 140 (PDF p. 6), Figure 3 panel A discussion

p.location: Journal p. 140 (PDF p. 6), Figure 3 panel A discussion
p.quote:
While only 11 percent of less educated Trump supporters chose the wrong
                image as having more people, 26 percent of Trump supporters with college
                degrees selected the incorrect photo (difference of proportions p = .054).

replication.target_description: Study 1, exploratory Hypothesis 14: among 2016 Trump voters, college education predicts incorrect selection of the crowd-size photo; chi-square test.

n.sample_role: 2016 Trump-voter participants in the post-exclusion sample; subgroup for Hypothesis 14.
n.exclusions: Excluded survey duration <5 or >60 minutes, age <18 or >100, duplicate IP, and non-USA IP; complete data for 1018 before exclusions.

reported_success.quote: We did not find evidence for this hypothesis

notes:
Replication p. 6 locator identifies Hypothesis 14 among Trump voters. The related education analysis among Republicans is Hypothesis 7 on pp. 5–6 (χ²(1) = 0.206, p = .650); it is a distinct sample/test and was not merged. Original paper unavailable. Printed chi-square retained without conversion to OR. Subgroup n is explicitly printed in post-exclusion Materials; no further test-specific exclusions reported.
Source follow-up: Original-only blind validation. Published 2018 article, DOI/title/authors verified in supplied primary text. PDF target pages visually inspected; printed journal pages 139–141 correspond to PDF pages 5–7. Canonical text agrees with rendered numeric values; original line-break hyphenation is retained in quotes. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Requested OR is not printed; the paper reports group percentages and a difference-of-proportions p without a numerical contrast statistic. No odds ratio was calculated. Figure 2 gives 218 Trump voters for the overall first-condition group, but Figure 3 does not print education-subgroup n or establish the precise analytic sample for the education comparison; n remains null. The p = .025 on p. 141 concerns education among strong Trump approvers, a different subgroup, and was not substituted. No Republican-only analysis is identified.
